# NPDO design system

## 1 · Identity

- Project: NPDO (`npdo`)
- Design system: NPDO, status draft

### Principles (draft)

One heading per principle; each heading is a link target (`text:principles#<heading>`).

**Readable at a glance**

The information a player needs right now reads in under a second at the smallest target resolution.

**Quiet until needed**

Chrome is dim and translucent; screens fade in with staggered 500-1600 ms ease-out opacity timelines, so the background art and the game stay in front.

**Warm monochrome, one red**

Near-black ground and one bone / cream ramp carry all type, rules and highlights. The only saturated colours are meaning: blood red for danger and for the single emphasised word (處分), sage for safe status. Never decorate with colour.

**Paperwork in the ruins**

The player is a government officer on a site survey, not an explorer: the story bible makes the job, the agency and the word 處分 (disposal) the frame of the game. Chrome borrows from survey forms: ruled lines, labelled fields, small caps-like tracking, form-style headings, so the UI feels like an official instrument inside a decaying place.

**Dread first, defiance later**

The game has two registers. Route 1 is survival (hold your breath, hide your fear): the UI stays quiet, dim and sparse, and nothing on screen is louder than the player's own fear. Route 2 turns the fear around ("the ghosts should fear you"): the same chrome may grow louder (warmer light, the one red used more boldly, punchier motion) but keeps its structure. Design every screen for Route 1 first; Route 2 is a variant of it, not a new look.

**Respect the safe area**

Anchored elements sit inside the safe area (2.5 % default, 5 % console) on the 1280 x 720 logical canvas. Title and copy stay in the top-left and bottom-right corners, as in the key art; the centre belongs to the scene.

**Immediate feedback**

Hover and selected states answer within 140-160 ms (ease-out) and always change contrast, not only colour.

### World (draft)

Summary of the story bible (`ref:story/npdo-story-zh`, English: `ref:story/npdo-story-en`). The UI should feel like it belongs to this world; it does not tell the story.

**Premise**

The player is an officer of the National Property Administration (國有財產署) who disposes of state land. The assignment: survey a hospital on land leased by a dissolved legal entity (built 1991, abandoned 1997) and decide how to dispose of it. The survey turns into imprisonment.

**The hospital**

Two connected buildings: the Surgical Building (cardiac surgery) and the Internal Medicine & Psychosomatic Medicine Building (frontier treatments). Funded by a foundation; sealed since a failed hostage rescue twenty years ago.

**What is inside**

Obsessions left by experiments on bio-energy (生體能量) run as a cult-like project for control; monsters twisted in mind and body; intruders assimilated and fused; and ghosts that were always there.

**Two routes**

Route 1: survive. Hold your breath, hide your fear, evade, solve mechanisms, learn the past, get out. Route 2: fight back. "The ghosts should fear you."

**Open questions**

- Hospital name and city: the UI shows "St. Ren Hospital / Taipei" (聖仁醫院), the story bible names neither.
- Dates: abandoned 1997, incident "twenty years ago": when is the game set?
- Is Route 2 a separate route, a later phase or a mode? Item text changes with it.

### Voice (draft)

How the UI speaks: tone, capitalisation, numbers and localisation notes.

**Tone**

Procedural and understated, like a government survey that has met something it cannot file. Short declarative lines ending in a full stop, one emphasised word at the end. Atmospheric lines are one sentence ("Balance the hospital's silence against everything that breaks it."); actions are plain verbs. This is the Route 1 register. Route 2 may break into defiant, darkly comic exclamation ("Rise up! Let your rage burn!"), but system UI (menus, settings, prompts) keeps the Route 1 voice in both routes.

**Item descriptions**

First person, the officer speaking; wry and deadpan. The mundane is described with over-precise, almost clinical detail (the Glock as "a primer, a copper case, a cone of special alloy and smokeless powder"), and the punchline comes last. Wordplay on 處分 (disposal) is house style. An item's line can change with the route (Junk), so item text is per route. Puns that do not survive translation (嘴砲, "mouth cannon") carry a localisation note; see `ref:story/npdo-story-en`.

**Vocabulary**

Official language over game language: survey (勘查) rather than explore, disposal (處分) rather than kill or clear, case, site, date, surveyor. Place and organisation names follow `text:glossary`.

**Capitalisation**

English: Title Case for menu items, tabs and buttons (New Game, Load Game, Reset to Defaults). UPPERCASE for HUD labels and the location block. Sentence case for descriptions and prompts. Chinese has no case; use wide tracking for titles and labels instead.

**Numbers**

Volumes are integers 0-100 (rounded). The HUD clock is 24-hour HH:MM. Versions read vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Years use a spaced hyphen (1991 - 1997). Bars carry no unit.

**Localisation**

The story bible is written in Traditional Chinese (`ref:story/npdo-story-zh`), so zh-TW is the source language and English is a translation (`ref:story/npdo-story-en`; decision:0003). The UI is English only today and spec.languages is empty. Georgia has no CJK glyphs; a Traditional Chinese serif is needed (type:cjk-serif). Check label columns (about 280 px) and the HUD clusters with Chinese strings.

## 5 · Space and shape

### Space and shape

Logical canvas 1280 x 720. Edges are square: 1 px hairline borders (`line-*` swatches), radius 3 px on key caps, full radius only on the settings switch.

**Rhythm**

Gaps of 2, 4, 6, 10, 14 and 26 px are used; rows are 40 px, tabs 44 px, menu items 42 px, inventory slots 62 x 70 px. Screen edges keep 28-40 px of padding inside the safe area.

## 6 · Motion

### Motion

Only opacity is animated. All curves are ease-out.

**Entrance**

Every UI plays an `intro` timeline on show. Main menu: background 0-1200 ms, title 300-1300 ms, list 900-1600 ms. HUD: five clusters staggered by 100-200 ms (objective 0, location 200, vitals 300, prompt 400, inventory 500 ms), each fading over about 500-800 ms. Settings: tab strip 0-500 ms, panel 150-650 ms. The motion lint expects a 40-80 ms stagger; the HUD uses 100-200 ms (see lint motion.entrance.stagger).

**Hover**

Menu items and hint chips respond in 140-160 ms (opacity or colour), tabs and rows 140-160 ms (background colour).

## 7 · Layout

### Safe area

- Default: 2.5 % of the viewport
- Console: 5 % of the viewport

## 9 · Imagery

### Imagery

**Key art**

Two reference key arts set the look: the exterior of St. Ren Hospital at dusk (`ref:key-art/af3f1d8f-b44b-402c-8232-d975d9c177a8`) and a ward corridor with a lit doorway (`ref:key-art/d5b9776d-3c07-4237-835b-f79ffc258b9c`).

- Photoreal, desaturated, wet and overgrown; near-black shadows (about 35 % of the exterior is #060605, another 17 % #161715), cold blue-grey with one warm light source.
- Foreground is dark and out of focus (clipboard, rusted gate) to frame the scene; the subject sits right of centre.
- Text lives in three places only: title lockup top-left (NPDO, 國有財產處置員, English line), tagline below it, and an optional lore blurb bottom right. The red word (處分) is the only colour accent.
- Props that recur and may become icons: the 國有財產署 現地勘查紀錄 clipboard form, ward signage with arrows, a floor directory (RF to B2), the green cross of the hospital sign.

**Assets in the project**

- `menu-bg` (1672 x 941): intro key art, used by the main menu and the settings screen.
- `menu-title` (2172 x 724, alpha): game title logo.
- `hud-preview-bg` (1536 x 1024): in-game still used only as a HUD preview backdrop; not shipped art.

Art is darkened by the side and bottom shades so text stays above contrast; never place text on the bare image.

## 10 · Screens

### In-game HUD (draft)

Minimal survival HUD over the game view. In the game it is transparent: the preview background and the corner vignette are `editor-only`.

- Top left: objective. Top right: location and clock. Right middle: interact prompt.
- Bottom left: health, stamina and noise meters. Bottom right: four inventory slots.
- Values: objective, location, clock, hp, stamina, noise_label, interact_label, interact_visible, all with defaults.

**Fit with the story**

- The stamina and noise meters carry Route 1 (hold your breath, hide your fear): noise is the most important reading after health.
- The inventory placeholders (Flashlight, Crowbar, Clipboard, East Wing Key) only partly match the story bible's items (unlock items, Junk, Crowbar, Glock, MP5, a "memento"). Route 2 weapons will need an ammo or charge readout that the HUD does not have yet.
- Location names should use the two buildings: Surgical Building and Internal Medicine Building (`text:glossary`).

Full spec: `ref:rebuild/hud-spec`; screenshots `ref:screens/hud`, `ref:screens/hud-variant-low-hp`.

### Main menu (draft)

Entry screen over the intro key art with the game title and a six-item list (New Game, Continue, Load Game, Options, Credits, Quit).

- Left and bottom shades keep the list readable over the art; rain, low fog, a flickering street lamp and edge grime keep the scene alive.
- Items fade in last (900-1600 ms) after a title glitch at about 1.25 s; hover slides in a textured smoky band with a muted blood-red edge and makes the label flicker.
- Ports: new_game, continue_game, load_game, open_options, open_credits, quit_game (events out).
- Key hints bottom right: W / S select, E confirm.

Full spec: `ref:rebuild/main-menu-spec`; screenshots `ref:screens/main-menu`, `ref:screens/main-menu-hover-options`.

### Rebuild brief (draft)

The first build of the three screens was captured on 2026-10-18 and then removed, to be rebuilt from this design document. Rebuild from these references; the look and behaviour are the target, the old structure is not.

| What | Reference |
|---|---|
| Project frame, assets, screen flow, lessons learned | `ref:rebuild/npdo-ui-rebuild-overview` |
| Main menu (layers, item hover, intro, ambient idle / rain / fog) | `ref:rebuild/main-menu-spec` |
| Settings (tab strip, six panels, row controls, footer, values) | `ref:rebuild/settings-spec` |
| In-game HUD (five clusters, values, intro) | `ref:rebuild/hud-spec` |
| Screenshots | `ref:screens/main-menu`, `main-menu-intro-0-5s`, `main-menu-intro-1-27s-glitch`, `main-menu-hover-options`, `settings-tab0` to `settings-tab5`, `settings-hover-tab`, `settings-hover-row`, `hud`, `hud-variant-low-hp` |
| Textures (copies of `shared/img`) and their recipe | `ref:assets/*`, `ref:assets/texture-recipe-tex2` |

**Order**

1. Main menu first, then settings, then the HUD; wire the screen flow (main menu -> settings / HUD, settings Back -> main menu) as soon as two screens exist.
2. After each screen, check it in the editor's Demo space starting from the main menu, not only on the canvas: the first build looked right on the canvas but not in Demo.
3. Preview-only backdrops are `editor-only`; the published UIs are transparent except the main menu's own key art.

### Settings (draft)

Tab strip (Gameplay, Graphics, Audio, Controls, Accessibility, Microphone) beside a 560 px content panel, footer with Apply (A), Reset to Defaults (R), Back (B / Escape). In the game it sits over whatever is behind it: the key-art background and its shade are `editor-only`, and the tab strip, panel and footer carry their own translucent dark surfaces.

- Every tab has a panel; Audio is the designed one, the others hold placeholder rows (sliders and switches work, choice boxes are static).
- The selected tab and the hovered tab use the same textured band as the main menu.
- Every value is a port with a default; Reset to Defaults writes the defaults back.

Full spec: `ref:rebuild/settings-spec`; screenshots `ref:screens/settings-tab0` to `ref:screens/settings-tab5`.
